notes: COVERAGE IS INCOMPLETE. All seven planned web searches were refused (shared search budget exhausted), including the required ones on superintelligence, extinction or existential risk, pause or moratorium, China agreement, and "AI safety"; none ran. Instead I opened pages directly and used news sites' own search pages (listed in `searches`); these site searches only showed the first page of results and matched loosely. Pages I could not open: the WTTW News interview of 6 April 2026 (https://news.wttw.com/2026/04/06/lt-gov-juliana-stratton-her-us-senate-campaign-health-care-funding-and-raising-minimum), which Wikipedia cites for her technology positions (rate-limited, then HTTP 403); WTTW site search; Chicago Tribune and Politico (fetch blocked); Daily Herald search and Ballotpedia (returned empty pages). The second pamphlet (Affordability Blueprint) could not be read as text and was not checked. All three quotes come from one written questionnaire answer, read at source and checked character for character against the page; the date is the publication date of the questionnaire (17 February 2026). The same answer does not mention safety, catastrophic risk, superintelligence, weapons, China, or a pause. Paraphrase left out: Capitol News Illinois (8 December 2025) reports that her housing plan includes "restricting the ability of artificial intelligence to set rents and screen applicants" (reporter's words, not hers). No AI mention found in: Capitol News Illinois report on the only Stratton-Tracy forum (21 October 2026), its report on the second Democratic primary debate (29 January 2026), the WBEZ profile of 8 November 2026, the campaign site home and issues pages, or the lieutenant governor's site (which lists no press releases). 23 September 2026 letter on AI talks with China and the Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act: she was not a senator at the time, so could not have signed or co-sponsored; I found no source showing her commenting on either, but the searches that would test this did not run.
